architecture_decisions.decision: Implement source mutation as additive code/patching.py and code/implementation.py modules that accept an explicit filesystem workspace root and expose no shell, Git, network, provider, or deployment authority.
Use a strict single-target unified-diff parser with exact SHA-256 pre-image binding and deterministic observable before/after evidence.

Separate preparation from mutation, bound per-file and aggregate source/patch/result resources, prepare all targets first, then commit atomically per file with rollback of prior writes on later failure.

work_items.action: Implement immutable patch request/prepared-patch contracts, safe path validation, UTF-8/target policy, strict unified diff parsing/application, no-op rejection, resource bounds, deterministic evidence, atomic commit, and restoration helpers.

Implement the multi-file SafeImplementationEngine that rejects duplicate targets, prepares every patch before mutation, enforces aggregate source/patch/result limits, commits in deterministic order, rolls back committed targets on failure, and returns artifact/workspace evidence without claiming release authority.

Add focused positive and protected-negative patch tests for valid modification/creation, traversal, symlink escape, malformed or mismatched diff, stale base, hunk mismatch, no-op patches, unsupported/binary/secret-sensitive targets, and resource bounds.

Add protected spec/plan validation plus multi-file success, deterministic evidence, duplicate-target, prepare-before-mutate, aggregate-source/patch/result bounds, and simulated later-commit rollback tests.

validations.check: Run the repository protected specification evaluators against specs/P2-V0.14.2.md and specs/compiled/P2-V0.14.2.plan.json and require PASS.

Run the relevant repository API regression and protected CI gates on the worker PR; verify the diff does not touch autonomy.py, service.py, sandbox_execution.py, state_machine.py, shared API wiring, or deployment workflows.

risks.risk: Unified diff edge cases could be interpreted inconsistently.
risks.mitigation: Support a deliberately strict subset and reject unsupported, multi-file, no-op, or ambiguous syntax instead of guessing.

risks.risk: Filesystem symlinks or special files could redirect writes outside the workspace or into unsafe targets.
risks.mitigation: Reject symlink components and non-regular existing targets, enforce lexical/resolved workspace containment, and re-check before commit.

risks.risk: A target can change between preparation and commit or a later write can fail after earlier commits.
risks.mitigation: Revalidate the pre-image before commit and roll back prior commits; never report protected success when commit or rollback fails.

risks.risk: Attacker-controlled patch/file volume could cause excessive memory or evidence growth.
risks.mitigation: Enforce per-patch, per-source, per-result, request-count, aggregate-source, aggregate-patch, and aggregate-result limits without invoking external processes.

risks.risk: This worker could invent a Project identity that conflicts with #43 or couple prematurely to autonomy internals.
risks.mitigation: Use only an explicit workspace root in the standalone engine and defer durable project/IMPLEMENT wiring to serialized integration.
